clue.text: Collar head of Yard easily remembered?

parts.note: to collar a suspect is to catch them

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, so only the start of Yard is used

explanation.surface: A police arrest made by the boss of Scotland Yard, memorable enough to talk about.
explanation.definitionFit: A tune that sticks in the head is called catchy; the question mark marks a loose, playful definition.

clue.text: Bash clue about something a priest gets into?

indicators.note: about means moved around, so the letters of these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone attacking a crossword clue and turning it about to find what a priest wears.
explanation.definitionFit: A chasuble is the sleeveless outer vestment a priest puts on to celebrate Mass.

clue.text: Labour's leader unseated in this?

parts.note: recalls the 2016 episode when Labour leader Jeremy Corbyn sat on the floor of a crowded rail carriage, complaining he could find no seat

explanation.surface: A political question about where the party leader lost his place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unseated' suggests losing an election, but here it means literally without a seat: a packed railway carriage. Labour is one of Britain's two main political parties.
explanation.definitionFit: A crowded railway service is the place where a standing passenger has no seat.

clue.text: A particular role that requires no top

indicators.note: requires no top tells us to drop the first letter of the word that

explanation.surface: A job description saying the post needs no senior figure above it.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: wearing one's teacher's or manager's headgear means acting in that particular role.

clue.text: Ciphers broken by males with no things to go on

indicators.note: broken by means the first word is split open with other letters placed inside

parts.note: ciphers are codes
M is the abbreviation for male, doubled for the plural
O, a nought, stands for no or nothing

explanation.surface: Secret messages cracked by men who have nothing to go on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Things to go on' sounds like clues for codebreakers, but means seats to relieve oneself on.
explanation.definitionFit: A commode is a chair housing a chamber pot, something one sits on to go to the toilet.

clue.text: Altogether done with a vacuous liberal

parts.note: something done or finished is over

indicators.note: vacuous means empty, so the inside is removed and only the outer letters of liberal remain

explanation.surface: Someone completely finished with an empty-headed liberal.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are adverbs meaning in total or taken as a whole.

clue.text: Top boys I muddle up

indicators.note: up as in stirred up: the letters of the words before it are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A boast from someone who is the best at confusing young lads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' looks like an adjective meaning best but is a garment. The anagram indicator is 'up', with 'muddle' part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A middy blouse is a loose sailor-collared garment worn on the upper body, a kind of shirt.

clue.text: Some clobber crap a soothsayer put about

parts.note: crap, vulgarly, is dung

indicators.note: put about means turned round, so the soothsayer word is written backwards

parts.note: a soothsayer is a seer

explanation.surface: A fortune-teller spreading rubbish about someone's clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: Clobber is British slang for clothes or gear. 'Put about' turns SEER into REES.
explanation.definitionFit: Dungarees are bib-and-brace work trousers, one item of clothing or gear.

clue.text: Spirits crack without topside of roast (and seconds)

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the crack word goes around a letter

parts.note: to have a crack at something is to have a shot

indicators.note: topside is a cut of beef, but here the top or first letter of roast

explanation.surface: A recipe: topside of beef roasted, with second helpings and some spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topside' is a British cut of beef, which suits the roast picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Shorts is the pub term for small measures of spirits such as whisky or gin.

clue.text: Restriction regarding cuddling Soprano in bed

indicators.note: in means placed inside the bed word

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

indicators.note: cuddling means wrapping round, so one piece holds another

parts.note: RE means regarding, as in a letter heading
S is the abbreviation for soprano in music

explanation.surface: A rule about cuddling a singer in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soprano' and 'in bed' paint a romantic scene, but the answer is an undergarment; 'cuddling' and 'in' are both container signals, one nested inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A tight foundation garment restricts the body, and figuratively the word means any constraint.

clue.text: In one action, anatomist gutted a butterfly?

indicators.note: gutted means the insides are taken out, leaving only the first and last letters of anatomist

parts.note: butterfly is a swimming stroke

explanation.surface: A dissector disembowelling a butterfly in a single movement.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means with a single blow or action, all at once.

clue.text: Clamour over detaining German dog

indicators.note: detaining means holding something inside, so the other letters enclose a letter

parts.note: clamour is a din
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A noisy fuss over a German dog being held, as at a quarantine kennel.
explanation.definitionFit: The dingo is the wild dog of Australia, a type of canine.

clue.text: Nuns see racy jiggling more than is called for

indicators.note: jiggling means shaking about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Nuns watching something saucy jiggling about, which seems excessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Something needless or superfluous goes beyond what is required.

clue.text: Something one prizes most? Meat and two veg!

definitions.meaning: the most treasured possession, like the regalia kept at the Tower of London
British slang for the male genitals, borrowed from the traditional plain dinner

explanation.walkthrough: 'Meat and two veg' is a classic British dinner of a meat with two vegetables, and comic slang for the male private parts; the gem-studded regalia sense is another slang name for the same.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both the most precious possessions and, in slang, a man's genitals.

clue.text: Do behave

definitions.meaning: to do something is to perform or take action
to behave in a certain way is to conduct oneself

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to perform or take action, and also to conduct oneself in a given way.

clue.text: Yob going round tree to spend a penny or two?

indicators.note: going round means one word encloses another

parts.note: a yob is a lout
the ash is a tree

explanation.surface: A hooligan relieving himself behind a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spend a penny' is British slang for using the toilet, which suits the yob by the tree; here it means spending money freely, with tongue in cheek.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to spend extravagantly; the question mark admits that a penny or two is ironic.

clue.text: An accessory of criminal in stir gets brief

indicators.note: criminal suggests something bent or crooked, so these letters are rearranged
brief means cut short, so the last letter of gets is dropped

explanation.surface: A criminal accomplice who gets a short sentence in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stir' is slang for prison and 'accessory' for an accomplice, but the accessory is a garment. 'Brief' cuts GETS to GET, which joins IN STIR in the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow necktie, often tied in a bow, is a dress accessory.

clue.text: I lie lazily about learner luxury cars clipped

definitions.note: the definition speaks as the answer: one who sprawls idly

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate

indicators.note: clipped means trimmed at both ends, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: Rollers is slang for Rolls-Royce cars

explanation.surface: A learner driver taking a luxury car out and clipping it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clipped' trims ROLLERS to OLLER. The definition is in the first person, the answer describing itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who lolls is a lounger who sprawls idly about.

clue.text: Tart needles on and off, but also flatters

parts.note: a flan is an open tart

indicators.note: on and off means taking letters alternately, starting with the first of needles

explanation.surface: A tart who teases and also flatters intermittently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On and off' picks N, E, L, S from needles.
explanation.definitionFit: To flannel is to use smooth, flattering talk to win someone over.

clue.text: You mostly called America another world

parts.note: U is text-speak for you

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter is used

parts.note: called on the phone is rang
the US is America

explanation.surface: Someone who phoned America and reached a different world.
explanation.definitionFit: Uranus is a planet, another world besides ours in the solar system.

clue.text: Fielder that's a victim of icy conditions?

definitions.meaning: in cricket, a fielder stationed in the slips beside the wicketkeeper

definitions.text: that's a victim of icy conditions?
definitions.meaning: one who slides and falls on ice

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the slips are close catching positions next to the wicketkeeper.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a cricketer in the slips and, playfully, anyone who skids on ice.

clue.text: Advice on clues in need of a new approach

indicators.text: in need of a new approach
indicators.note: needing a new approach means these letters must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Guidance for a stuck solver: tackle the clues differently.
explanation.definitionFit: Counsel is guidance or recommendation given to someone.

clue.text: Bend over barrel for a potential strangler!

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the bend word is written backwards

parts.note: a bend is an arc
a vat is a large barrel

explanation.surface: An order to bend over a barrel from someone who sounds menacing.
explanation.definitionFit: A cravat is a neckcloth tied round the throat, so in jest it could throttle the wearer.

clue.text: Baron working to ensnare Hood in Nottingham

parts.note: a machine that is working is on
to ensnare is to net

explanation.surface: A Norman baron scheming to trap Robin Hood near Nottingham.
explanation.walkthrough: Robin Hood is the outlaw of Nottingham legend, but 'Hood' is the American word for the engine cover that the British, as in Nottingham, call by another name.
explanation.definitionFit: The British term for a car's engine cover is the same thing Americans call the hood.

clue.text: Private parts essential to wow and awe one

indicators.note: the essential part of a word is its centre, so the middle letter of each of the three words is taken

explanation.surface: Intimate body parts said to be vital for impressing and astonishing someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Private parts' reads as one phrase, but splits into the definition and the start of the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Something private belongs to one person alone, as in a room of one's own.

clue.text: Bacon for one table, in haze, gets mixed up

indicators.note: mixed up means these letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Breakfast bacon on a hazy, muddled table.
explanation.walkthrough: Bacon looks like the breakfast meat but is Francis Bacon, philosopher and statesman under Elizabeth I.
explanation.definitionFit: Francis Bacon lived and wrote in the reign of Elizabeth I, so he is an example of a figure of that era.

clue.text: Heroin, unlimited tabs and sex can form one

definitions.text: Heroin, unlimited tabs and sex can form one

parts.note: H is slang for heroin

indicators.note: unlimited means the outer letters are removed, leaving the middle of tabs

parts.note: it is a euphemism for sex

explanation.surface: A warning that drugs, pills and sex can become an addiction.
explanation.definitionFit: An addiction is a compulsive habit, which drugs and sex can both become.

clue.text: Some beer tins spun round can be explosive stuff

indicators.note: spun round means the selected letters are read backwards
some means only part of the words beer tins is used

explanation.surface: Beer cans spun around may explode when opened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes ERTIN from beer tins; 'spun round' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Saltpetre, potassium nitrate, is a key ingredient of gunpowder, so an explosive substance.

clue.text: Board in pursuit of proposal fit for cultivation

indicators.note: in pursuit of means following, so this piece comes after the other

parts.note: a proposal is a plan
a board is a table

explanation.surface: A company board chasing a proposal suitable for development.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground that can take seeds or saplings is suited to growing crops.

clue.text: Hero of Robert Burns? 'Twas me on occasion!

indicators.note: on occasion means now and then, so every other letter is taken, starting with the first

explanation.surface: The poet's hero claiming he was the one in the tale.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Burns, Scotland's national poet, wrote 'Tam o' Shanter', whose title character gives his name to a Scottish cap.
explanation.definitionFit: Tam is the hero of the Burns poem; the question mark hints it is also the bonnet named after him.

clue.text: Step away from date? Certainly, darling

indicators.note: away from means the date letter is taken out

parts.note: a step is a tread
sure means certainly

explanation.surface: Someone backing out of a romantic date, reassuring a sweetheart.
explanation.definitionFit: A loved and valued person can be called a treasure, a term of endearment.

clue.text: Hoskins is involved in groups backing strikes

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the whole assembly is reversed
involved in means placed within the groups word

parts.note: groups are sets
Hoskins is the setter, who would say I am, shortened to I'm

explanation.surface: The setter joining trade unions in support of strike action.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often refer to themselves by name, so 'Hoskins is' stands for 'I'm'. 'Backing' turns the whole assembled SETIMS round, not just the groups.
explanation.definitionFit: To smite is an old word for to hit hard, so smites means strikes.
